$comment: Exception register for known npm advisories. Every entry requires an owner, exposure analysis, mitigation, and review date per docs/production-roadmap.md milestone M0. CI fails when an unreviewed advisory appears or when an entry no longer matches the audit result.
reviewCadence: Re-review every entry after each Expo SDK step in docs/decisions/0001-expo-sdk-upgrade-path.md, and at minimum every 30 days.

advisories.title: braces vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns
advisories.exposure: Build-time only. Reached through micromatch in jest-haste-map and metro-file-map, which run in Node during `npm test`, bundling, and CI. The vulnerable code is not part of the JavaScript bundle shipped to iOS or Android.
advisories.risk: A glob pattern with pathological nesting could stall a developer machine or a CI runner. The patterns come from Expo, Metro, and Jest configuration in this repository, not from user input at runtime.
advisories.mitigation: Pinned input: repository glob configuration is committed and reviewed, and CI runs with a job timeout. Upgrade path is the Expo SDK sequence in docs/decisions/0001-expo-sdk-upgrade-path.md.

advisories.title: image-size: JXL and HEIF parsers allow denial of service through infinite loops
advisories.exposure: Build-time only. Used by the Expo asset pipeline in @expo/cli and expo-asset on Node while bundling. Not shipped to the device runtime. This does not change the M3 requirement to normalize and validate every upload in a quarantined server-side worker.
advisories.risk: A decompression-bomb or malformed JXL/HEIF asset added in a pull request could hang the bundler or CI runner.
advisories.mitigation: Contributor-supplied image assets are treated as untrusted input, so CI jobs are isolated and time-limited. Future server-side sanitization is specified in docs/production-roadmap.md milestone M3.

advisories.title: image-size: ICNS parser allows denial of service through an infinite loop
advisories.exposure: Build-time only, same image-size asset pipeline as advisory 1239765. Not part of the shipped bundle.
advisories.risk: A malformed icon asset could hang the bundler or CI runner.
advisories.mitigation: Assets are version-controlled and reviewed, and CI jobs are time-limited.

advisories.title: node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements
advisories.exposure: Build-time only. Reached through @expo/code-signing-certificates in @expo/cli, which is used for EAS code signing on Node. CatMap does not verify arbitrary third-party RSA signatures with this library today.
advisories.risk: A crafted certificate or signature could pass verification during a signing step. Requires an attacker to influence build inputs or the signing service response.
advisories.mitigation: Signing credentials are supplied by EAS through CI environment variables and are never committed. Rotate signing credentials if the dependency is ever used to validate untrusted input.

advisories.title: PostCSS: Arbitrary file read and information disclosure via attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL in CSS comments
advisories.exposure: Build-time only. Used by the Metro CSS pipeline through @expo/metro-config on Node while bundling. Not shipped to the device runtime.
advisories.risk: A stylesheet or node_modules change in a pull request could read files from the bundling machine, which is the highest-value residual risk in this register because CI runners hold secrets.
advisories.mitigation: Pull requests from forks run without repository secrets, secret scanning is enforced in CI, and workflows grant read-only permissions. Remove this entry as soon as the Expo upgrade resolves it.

advisories.title: PostCSS: Path Traversal in Previous Source Map Auto-Loading (sourceMappingURL) leads to Arbitrary .map File Disclosure
advisories.exposure: Build-time only, same PostCSS and Metro path as advisory 1124252.
advisories.risk: A stylesheet change could disclose map files from the build machine.
advisories.mitigation: Fork pull requests run without secrets, and secret scanning blocks accidental commits.

advisories.title: PostCSS has XSS via Unescaped </style> in its CSS Stringify Output
advisories.exposure: Build-time only. Generated CSS is written to the bundle, not served as a standalone stylesheet to browsers.
advisories.risk: Minimal for a React Native bundle that has no browser CSS parsing surface.
advisories.mitigation: No action required beyond tracking; the upgrade removes it.

advisories.title: PostCSS: incomplete fix of GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q, attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL reads arbitrary .map files when from is unset
advisories.exposure: Build-time only, same PostCSS and Metro path as advisory 1124252.
advisories.risk: A stylesheet change could read source map files from the build machine.
advisories.mitigation: Fork pull requests run without secrets, and secret scanning blocks accidental commits.

advisories.title: esbuild allows arbitrary file read when running the development server on Windows
advisories.exposure: Development server only, and only on Windows. CatMap developers use macOS and Linux, and the development server is never exposed publicly.
advisories.risk: Windows contributors running a shared-network development server could expose local files.
advisories.mitigation: Documented so any future Windows contributor binds the Metro server to localhost only.

advisories.title: sprintf-js vulnerable to denial of service through unbounded precision specifiers
advisories.exposure: Build-time only, reached through argparse in the React Native community CLI on Node. Not shipped to the device runtime.
advisories.risk: A crafted CLI argument could stall a build. Arguments come from committed npm scripts.
advisories.mitigation: No runtime exposure; the upgrade removes it.

advisories.title: uuid: Missing buffer bounds check in v3/v5/v6 when buf is provided
advisories.exposure: Build-time only, reached through @expo/cli on Node. The app does not generate UUIDs with a caller-supplied buffer.
advisories.mitigation: No runtime exposure; the upgrade removes it.
